questions.scenarioContext: A connecting line is a component of a flowchart.
questions.prompt: Identify two other components of a flowchart.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: start/stop (terminator), process, decision, input/output, sub-routine, arrow/directional flow.

questions.prompt: Identify one display hardware consideration for a Human Computer Interface (HCI).
questions.markSchemeHint: Screen size, resolution, colour depth, orientation, aspect ratio, brightness/contrast, touchscreen.

questions.prompt: Which of these is formatted as an alphanumeric data type?
questions.markSchemeHint: C) 432BJ (1 mark).

questions.prompt: Which of these is not a secondary research source?
questions.markSchemeHint: B) Interview (1 mark).

questions.prompt: Identify one logical storage location.
questions.markSchemeHint: Cloud storage, network drive, local hard drive/folder/partition, server.

questions.prompt: Which type of test checks that a system will work on a device screen?
questions.markSchemeHint: Compatibility testing (or visual/display/usability/technical testing).

questions.prompt: Which of these hackers has permission to hack into a business computer system?
questions.markSchemeHint: C) White Hat (1 mark).

questions.prompt: Link each type of social engineering to the correct description. (You will only use two types of social engineering to complete the task.)
matchingLeft: Criminals promise goods to get the information they need
Criminals use computer programs designed to trick a user into buying and downloading unnecessary and dangerous software
questions.markSchemeHint: Baiting -> Criminals promise goods to get the information they need (1); Scareware -> Criminals use computer programs designed to trick a user into buying and downloading unnecessary and dangerous software (1).

questions.scenarioContext: Hackers have accessed a business database. Some of the stored data has been deleted.
questions.prompt: This is an example of?
questions.markSchemeHint: A) Data destruction (1 mark).

questions.scenarioContext: Keypads are one physical protection measure.
questions.prompt: Identify one other physical protection measure.
questions.markSchemeHint: Biometrics (fingerprint/iris/face scanner), RFID card/swipe pass, locks/keyed doors, CCTV, security guards, alarm/motion sensors, cable locks.

questions.prompt: Which legislation applies to employees using a computer system?
options: A) Copyright, Designs and Patents Act
D) Health and Safety at Work Act
questions.markSchemeHint: D) Health and Safety at Work Act (1 mark).

questions.prompt: Identify one type of distribution channel connectivity that could be used for digital communications.
questions.markSchemeHint: Wired (Ethernet/fibre), Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Mobile/Cellular (4G/5G), Satellite, NFC/RFID.

questions.prompt:
Complete the sentence:
When talking about the Internet of Everything (IoE), WWW stands for ...........................
questions.markSchemeHint: World Wide Web.

questions.figureNote: Fig. 1 on Page 5 shows a handwritten takeaway order: Name: Mia Taylor | Email: MT901@reur.co.uk | Meals: Beef pie with chips, Lasagna, Salad | Cost: £18.70 | Paid: Y | Order number: 2378 | Collection time: 19:15.
questions.scenarioContext: Monty Bella restaurant has a takeaway service. Customers telephone to order meals and orders are handwritten (Fig. 1: Name = Mia Taylor, Cost = £18.70, Paid = Y, Order number = 2378, Collection time = 19:15).
questions.prompt: Complete the table to show the data types that are used when entering the order onto a computer system. Justify your choice.
questions.markSchemeHint: 3 marks per row (1 data type + 2 justification): Name -> Text / String / Alphabetic (stores letters and spaces for customer names); Cost -> Currency (stores monetary values with £ sign and 2 decimal places for total calculations); Paid -> Boolean (only two values Yes/No or Y/N indicating whether payment is complete).

questions.scenarioContext: Storing Monty Bella customer orders.
questions.prompt: Describe one characteristic of an external solid-state drive that would make it suitable for Monty Bella to store the customer orders.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark characteristic + 1 mark contextual description: durable/no moving parts (safe in a busy kitchen/office), fast read/write speeds for quick order lookup, portable for off-site backup, high storage capacity.

questions.scenarioContext: Storing Monty Bella customer orders.
questions.prompt: Identify one logical storage location that could be used to store the customer orders.
questions.markSchemeHint: Cloud storage, network drive, or local hard drive/server.

questions.scenarioContext: Monty Bella is thinking about creating a website where customers can order takeaway meals and pay online. A Human Computer Interface (HCI) will be created as part of the website.
questions.prompt: Explain the purpose of a Human Computer Interface (HCI).
questions.markSchemeHint: Provides the visual/interactive link between the customer and the computer system (1) so users can easily input meal orders/payments and receive clear outputs/confirmations (1).

questions.scenarioContext: Customers of Monty Bella could use the HCI using the keyboard interaction method.
questions.prompt: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to the customers of using a keyboard to interact with the HCI.
questions.markSchemeHint: Advantage (2): fast and accurate for typing names, addresses, and email/card details; familiar to most users. Disadvantage (2): risk of typos/spelling mistakes; slower to navigate menus compared to mouse/touch; difficult for users with mobility impairments or on smartphones without physical keyboards.

questions.scenarioContext: Monty Bella takeaway website HCI.
questions.prompt: Identify one other interaction method that could be used with the HCI.
questions.markSchemeHint: Mouse, touch, voice, gesture, stylus/trackpad.

questions.scenarioContext: A validation tool that limits the user choice could be applied to the quantity of each meal that customers can order through the Monty Bella website.
questions.prompt: Explain why a limited choice validation tool will reduce errors when customers are ordering meals.
questions.markSchemeHint: Restricts customers to selecting only valid predefined numbers (e.g., drop-down 1–10) (1) so they cannot accidentally type letters, negative numbers, or unrealistic quantities like 100 meals (1).

questions.scenarioContext: Monty Bella restaurant is creating a new takeaway ordering website.
questions.prompt:
Create a mind map to plan the content for the homepage of Monty Bella's new takeaway website.
Marks will be awarded for: Content; Layout.
questions.markSchemeHint: Up to 4 marks Content (central node 'Monty Bella Homepage', branches for Menu/Order Online, Special Offers, Opening Hours & Location/Contact, Login/Register & Basket/Payment, Customer Reviews, House Style/Logo/Images) and up to 4 marks Layout (clear central idea, structured main branches and sub-branches, concise keywords, readable layout).

questions.scenarioContext: The Monty Bella restaurant website has been created and user testing has been carried out.
questions.prompt: Explain why user testing should be carried out on the website.
questions.markSchemeHint: To check how real customers navigate and order meals (1) so usability issues, confusing layouts, or broken ordering journeys are fixed before launch (1).

questions.scenarioContext: A leaflet has been created to advertise the takeaway service of Monty Bella restaurant and will be distributed by email to existing customers.
questions.prompt: Explain one advantage to the Monty Bella restaurant of using a leaflet to advertise the takeaway service.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark point + 1 mark expansion: eye-catching visual layout with meal photos/special offers grabs attention; summarises key menu/website details concisely; low design cost and easy to reuse digitally or in print.

questions.scenarioContext: Distributing the Monty Bella leaflet by email to existing customers.
questions.prompt: Explain one disadvantage to the customers of distributing the leaflet by email.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark point + 1 mark expansion: may go into spam/junk folder and be missed; requires internet/email access; large image attachments may load slowly or use mobile data; customers may worry about phishing/malware attachments.

questions.scenarioContext: Customers register with their name, address, phone number, and payment details, which are stored by the restaurant.
questions.prompt: Identify the legislation that relates to the storing of customer details.
questions.markSchemeHint: Data Protection Act (2018) / UK GDPR.

questions.scenarioContext: Complying with Data Protection legislation for customer details.
questions.prompt: Identify two actions that need to be taken by the restaurant to comply with the legislation.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: keep data secure (encryption/passwords), obtain customer consent, keep data accurate/up-to-date, do not keep data longer than necessary, only collect data needed for orders, do not share with third parties without permission.

questions.scenarioContext: When a customer registers for the Monty Bella website, they must create a username and password.
questions.prompt: Explain how the usernames and passwords will increase the security of the website.
questions.markSchemeHint: Verifies each customer's identity before granting access (1), preventing unauthorised users from viewing saved personal/payment details or placing fraudulent takeaway orders (1).

questions.scenarioContext: Monty Bella restaurant has been advised to install a firewall for its website.
questions.prompt: Explain how a firewall will increase the security of the Monty Bella website.
questions.markSchemeHint: Monitors and filters incoming and outgoing network traffic against security rules (1), blocking unauthorised access attempts, hackers, or malicious traffic from reaching the web server/customer database (1).

questions.scenarioContext: Monty Bella restaurant wants to collect feedback from its customers about the takeaway service using an online survey.
questions.prompt: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to the restaurant of using an online survey to collect the data.
questions.markSchemeHint: Advantage (2): quick and cheap to send to many customers, responses automatically stored/analysed into charts without manual typing. Disadvantage (2): low response rate (customers ignore links), biased/unreliable responses (mostly unhappy customers), excludes customers without internet.

questions.scenarioContext: Monty Bella restaurant uses a smart device connected to the Internet of Everything (IoE).
questions.prompt: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages to the restaurant of using a smart device connected to the Internet of Everything.
questions.markSchemeHint: OCR 9-mark Level of Response (L1: 1–3, L2: 4–6, L3: 7–9). Advantages: automates kitchen/restaurant tasks (smart fridge temperature alerts, automated stock reordering, smart lighting/heating saving energy, instant order display syncing, faster service & fewer mix-ups). Disadvantages: initial purchase/installation cost, relies on reliable Wi-Fi/internet and power, cyber-security vulnerabilities if smart devices are hacked, staff training/maintenance costs, potential job-role changes. Balanced discussion + conclusion.
